questions.title: Which DRC province will WHO identify as experiencing a surge in weekly Ebola cases in mid-September 2026?

questions.current_reasoning: Major Aug 17 DRC Ebola update across Bloomberg/Straits Times, Al Jazeera, and AFP/Korea Times: confirmed cases climbed to 4,945 (+101 in 24h) and deaths reached 2,325 (surpassing 2018-2020 to become Congo's deadliest outbreak ever), with UN relief chief Tom Fletcher warning the epidemic is doubling every 20 days. Crucially, Congo's National Institute of Public Health reported (Bloomberg/Straits Times Aug 17) that dedicated beds for suspected Ebola patients in North Kivu province reached 100% occupancy by Aug 15, forcing suspected cases across Butembo, Masereka, Vuhovi, and Kalunguta into ordinary non-designated health facilities where WHO warned Aug 14 nosocomial infection control is weakest (155 health workers infected, 45 killed). That urban hospital overflow creates a high-probability 3-4 week transmission surge landing squarely in the Sept 10-16 WHO window, lifting North Kivu 0.28 -> 0.32 into #1. Ituri holds 0.29 (epicenter in Bunia/Djugu/Nizi with >70% community deaths and ongoing worker strikes per WHO Africa director Mohamed Janabi Aug 17); Haut-Uele trims 0.30 -> 0.27 (still a major contender on rapid growth and 58% contact tracing); Bas-Uele stays 0.07 (sixth province reached via Buta index death Aug 13, secondary chains maturing into Sept); Tshopo trims 0.04 -> 0.03 (2% residual for South Kivu/Kinshasa/Maniema).

local_articles.title: Ebola is spreading faster beyond Congo epicentre, straining outbreak response
local_articles.snippet: unting pressure on efforts to trace and contain infections. Transmission is accelerating outside Ituri, where the epidemic began in early 2026. Confirmed cases increased at roughly double the pace in North Kivu and Haut- Uele provinces over the past week, while Tshopo recorded an even larger jump from a smaller base. The cumulative number of confirmed infections rose by 103 to 5,208 on Aug 18. The outbreak also expanded into another area in Bas- Uele province, bringing the number of affected health districts nationwide to 56, Congo’s Ministry for Communications and Media said on Aug 19. Congo has recorded 2,476 confirmed deaths, giving the outbreak a case-fatality rate of 47.5 per cent, it said.
